_meta.indication: OTEZLA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with active psoriatic arthritis

pivotal_trials.design: 24-week, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel group, multicenter study; subjects randomized 1:1:1 to apremilast 20 mg BID, apremilast 30 mg BID, or matching placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients (18 years and older) with active psoriatic arthritis despite prior or current DMARD therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving ACR20 response at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 16: apremilast 30 mg BID 38% vs placebo 19%

pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients (18 years and older) with active psoriatic arthritis despite prior or current DMARD therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving ACR20 response at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 16: apremilast 30 mg BID 32% vs placebo 19%

pivotal_trials.design: 24-week, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel group, multicenter study; subjects randomized 1:1:1 to apremilast 20 mg BID, apremilast 30 mg BID, or matching placebo. Study PsA-3 also required a qualifying psoriatic skin lesion.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients (18 years and older) with active psoriatic arthritis and a qualifying psoriatic skin lesion, despite prior or current DMARD therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving ACR20 response at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 16: apremilast 30 mg BID 41% vs placebo 18%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are diarrhea, nausea, and headache. In the placebo-controlled period diarrhea occurred in 9.3% and nausea 7.4% with OTEZLA 30 mg BID (Day 1-5). The most common adverse reactions leading to discontinuation were nausea (1.8%), diarrhea (1.8%), and headache (1.2%).
target_moa: Apremilast is an oral small-molecule inhibitor of phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) specific for cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP); PDE4 inhibition increases intracellular cAMP levels

rems.type: No post-marketing risk evaluation and mitigation strategies are recommended.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not convened for this application.

description.text: Expanded indication to include adult patients with plaque psoriasis who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy, adding data for mild to moderate plaque psoriasis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to the Indication and Usage, and Clinical Studies sections of the labeling to include data for subjects with mild to moderate plaque psoriasis, and to allow for an expansion of the indication to include adult patients with plaque psoriasis who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy. Additionally, a subsection entitled "Hypersensitivity" was added under the Warnings and Precautions section of the label.

summary.text: Standard full approval of apremilast (Otezla), the first small molecule drug approved for the treatment of adult patients with active psoriatic arthritis, based on three Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials; no advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required.

citations.quote: Apramilast is a phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) inhibitor. It will represent the first small molecule drug approved for the treatment of adult patients with active PsA.

An advisory committee was not convened for this application. The efficacy and safety finding for apremilast in the PsA clinical studies were clear and did not warrant discussion at an advisory committee meeting.
No post-marketing risk evaluation and mitigation strategies are recommended.
